follow-up time: January 2000 - December 2007 (audit) and July 2008 - October 2008 (pilot study)
exposure: women who used no pharmacological pain relief (control group)
women who used only subcutaneous fentanyl for pain relief
nitrous oxide and oxygen prior to subcutaneous fentanyl
women who used nitrous oxide and oxygen prior to being administered subcutaneous fentanyl
subcutaneous fentanyl for pain relief during labor
cohort: Pregnant women with uncomplicated pregnancies and term births (37-42 weeks gestation)
finding: While fentanyl use was associated with longer labor duration, likely due to higher induction rates, neonatal outcomes, length of hospital stay, and breastfeeding rates were comparable between groups.
mod_finding: The study found that the use of fentanyl for pain relief during labor was associated with longer labor duration and an increased likelihood of assisted vaginal birth, but did not affect neonatal outcomes.
